short: Japan's most famous duellist, who wrote the strategy book that outlasted him.
full:
Born about 1584, Musashi fought his first duel at thirteen and claimed some sixty victories without a defeat. He was present at Sekigahara in 1600, and later at the siege of Osaka and the suppression of the Shimabara Rebellion. His best known encounter came in 1612 on the islet of Ganryujima against Sasaki Kojiro, whom he killed with a wooden sword said to have been cut from a boat oar, having arrived deliberately late to unsettle him.

Musashi developed Niten Ichi-ryu, a two-sword style, and in later life was retained by the Hosokawa at Kumamoto. Withdrawing to a cave at Reigando, he wrote Go Rin no Sho, The Book of Five Rings, a short treatise on strategy finished shortly before his death on 13 June 1645. It has never gone out of print and is read far outside the martial arts. He was also a serious ink painter and calligrapher, and several of his works survive. Sabaton's "The Duelist", from Legends (2025), is about him.
